extracted.intended_audience: administrators and Title IX coordinators at K-12 schools, colleges, and universities; institutional legal/compliance staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural obligations that educational recipients of Federal funds must follow when they have actual knowledge of sexual harassment, including prompt responses, offering supportive measures, grievance processes, notice requirements, and investigatory/adjudicatory protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt response in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent
rubrics_metrics.description: When a recipient has actual knowledge of sexual harassment in its education program or activity, the recipient must respond promptly in a manner that is not deliberately indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that whether or not a formal complaint triggers a grievance process, the recipient must promptly offer supportive measures. The Department adapts the Gebser/Davis 'clearly unreasonable' standard to require a meaningful response to every report while allowing flexibility for context-specific decisions. A response that is 'not deliberately indifferent' must include specified mandatory steps (see other criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer supportive measures to complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer supportive measures to a complainant in response to a report of sexual harassment, regardless of whether a formal complaint is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supportive measures (defined in §106.30) are individualized services, reasonably available, without fee or charge, designed to restore or preserve a complainant's equal access to education. The Title IX Coordinator must engage in an interactive discussion to consider the complainant's wishes. Examples include different seating assignments, leaves of absence, accommodation for missed exams, or counseling/mental health services. Offering supportive measures is required even absent proof of allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator must contact complainant and consider wishes
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient's Title IX Coordinator must contact the complainant to discuss availability of supportive measures, consider the complainant's wishes regarding those measures, and explain the process for filing a formal complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interactive process must occur with or without the filing of a formal complaint; it gives complainants more control and choice (e.g., whether to receive supportive measures only, to file a formal complaint, or to pursue informal resolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not discipline respondent without following §106.45 grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must refrain from imposing disciplinary sanctions on a respondent until after complying with the grievance process set forth in §106.45.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treating complainants and respondents equitably means offering supportive measures to complainants while following the full grievance process prior to disciplining respondents. Where a respondent is found responsible, disciplinary decisions are within the recipient's discretion, but remedies to restore equal access must be provided as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably prompt time frame for conclusion of grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a formal complaint triggers a grievance process, the recipient must have a reasonably prompt time frame for the conclusion of the grievance process, including any appeals or informal resolution process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement appears in §106.45(b)(1)(v) and reflects the obligation to avoid unreasonably protracted proceedings; timeliness is part of a non-deliberately indifferent response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify and prominently post Title IX Coordinator contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must notify all students and employees (and parents/guardians of elementary and secondary school students) of the name or title, office address, email address, and telephone number of the employee(s) designated as the Title IX Coordinator, and must prominently display this contact information on their website and in handbooks/catalogs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures clear, accessible channels for reporting and that anyone knows to whom and how to report, including reporting options during non-business hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual knowledge definition and trigger for duties
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's duty to respond is triggered by 'actual knowledge' of sexual harassment or allegations thereof, defined as notice to the Title IX Coordinator, an official with authority to institute corrective measures, or any employee of an elementary/secondary school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person (not only the complainant) may report; recipients cannot avoid actual knowledge by willful ignorance. Once actual knowledge exists, the recipient must promptly offer supportive measures and take required steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education program or activity includes contexts under recipient's substantial control
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'education program or activity' includes locations, events, or circumstances over which the recipient exercised substantial control over both the respondent and the context in which the harassment occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that some off-campus incidents may be covered if the recipient had substantial control over the harasser and the context (e.g., recipient-provided housing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator may sign a formal complaint when circumstances warrant
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recipient has actual knowledge of a pattern or circumstances that justify it, the Title IX Coordinator may sign (file) a formal complaint obligating the recipient to investigate even if the complainant does not wish to file or participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision addresses situations (e.g., alleged harassment by someone in a position of authority) where action may be necessary despite a complainant's reluctance to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartial, trained personnel free from bias and conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel involved in investigations and adjudications must be free from bias and conflicts of interest and must be trained to serve impartially, without prejudgment of the facts and without bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.45(b)(1)(iii) and related provisions; training and impartiality are required for fair processes and meaningful participation by both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide meaningful opportunity to participate and evidence access
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a formal complaint triggers a grievance process, recipients must investigate and adjudicate in a way that gives both parties a meaningful opportunity to participate, including objectively evaluating relevant evidence, permitting parties to inspect and review evidence, and providing parties with a copy of the investigative report prior to any hearing or determination regarding responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural protections are part of §106.45 and are intended to produce accurate outcomes and protect due process for both complainants and respondents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory steps required in every response to sexual harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain steps are mandatory in all circumstances: promptly informing each complainant of the method for filing a formal complaint, offering supportive measures, and refraining from imposing disciplinary sanctions until the grievance process is followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed proposed 'safe harbor' provisions and replaced them with these specific obligations to ensure predictable, enforceable duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may use other conduct codes for non-Title IX conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If alleged conduct does not meet the Title IX definition of sexual harassment, the recipient may still take action under another provision of its code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicitly preserves recipients' ability to address misconduct outside the scope of Title IX through other institutional mechanisms (see §106.45(b)(3)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures must be reasonably available and tailored to keep complainant in school
rubrics_metrics.description: While supportive measures will vary among recipients, every recipient must be able to consider, offer, and provide some individualized services reasonably available and designed to help the complainant stay in school and on track academically and to protect safety or deter sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes that these are legal obligations requiring thoughtful, individualized responses, not mere paperwork; examples include academic accommodations and counseling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance does not require restricting constitutional rights
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient is not required to restrict a person's constitutional rights (including the First, Fifth, or Fourteenth Amendments) to satisfy its obligation not to be deliberately indifferent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.44(a) clarifies that protecting complainants' access does not justify unconstitutional restrictions; the Department will not deem a recipient compliant or non-deliberately indifferent solely on the basis of restricting constitutional rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department enforcement and expectation beyond 'check-the-box' compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will enforce these regulations and expects recipients to engage substantively (not merely 'check boxes')—informing complainants of options, offering supportive measures through interactive processes, and providing formal complaint processes with robust due process protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply will be handled as an enforcement matter; recipients must perform the detailed work required by the regulations (investigate, objectively evaluate evidence, permit evidence inspection, use trained impartial personnel).
